MCA Admission at BIT Jaipur 
Program Overview 
BIT Jaipur oƯers a Master of Computer Applications (MCA) program at its Jaipur campus 
for the 2026-27 academic year. This is a 2-year full-time postgraduate course that 
focuses on producing industry-ready professionals in computer applications and IT. 
The program is accredited by the National Board of Accreditation and is designed with a 
mix of core computer science subjects, practical lab work, and real-world industry 
experience. All students must complete a compulsory 6-month industry internship 
where they work at top IT companies across India. 
Important Dates for 2026 
 
Application Form Opens: 27 February 2026 
 
Last Date to Apply: 30 April 2026 (with a deadline extension to 31 May 2026) 
 
Mock Entrance Test: 30 May 2026 (Sunday, 10:00 AM to 12:00 Noon) 
 
Actual Entrance Test: 6 June 2026 to 13 June 2026 (Saturday, 10:00 AM to 12:00 
Noon) 
Note: These dates are tentative and may change. Check the oƯicial website regularly for 
updates. 
Who Can Apply? (Eligibility Criteria) 
To apply for MCA at BIT Jaipur, you must meet these requirements: 
Education Qualiﬁcation: 
 
You must have a Bachelor's degree (minimum 3 years after Class 12) from a 
recognized university in India 
Required Background: You must have one of these degrees: 
 
Bachelor of Computer Applications (BCA), OR 
 
B.Sc. in Computer Science, OR 
 
B.Sc. in Information Technology, OR 
 
B.Sc. in Computer Applications 
Minimum Marks: 
 
You need at least 55% average marks in your Bachelor's degree 
 
For SC/ST/PwD candidates: 50% average marks is acceptable 

 
If you studied Honours, the percentage is calculated based on Honours subjects 
only 
Special Conditions: 
 
Final Year Students: If you're appearing for your ﬁnal exams in 2026, you can 
apply provisionally if you have the required marks so far. You must submit your 
degree certiﬁcate by 31 October 2026 after passing. 
 
Distance Learning: If you studied through distance learning or correspondence, 
your program must be recognized by DEC-IGNOU and you must have already 
passed the course with required marks. 
 
Foreign Degrees: If you have a foreign degree, you need an equivalence 
certiﬁcate from AIU or EdCIL. 
How to Apply 
Follow these simple steps: 
1. Register Online: Click on "Apply Now" on the BIT Jaipur website to create your 
account and password. Keep this password safe. 
2. Fill Application Form: Complete the online application form with all your 
details. 
3. Choose Campus Preference: Select up to 3 campuses in order of preference. 
You cannot change this later. BIT Jaipur is one option available. 
4. Pay Application Fee: 
o General/OBC-NCL/EWS candidates: Rs. 1,500 
o SC/ST candidates: Rs. 1,000 
Pay through online banking, debit card, or credit card. Once paid, this fee cannot be 
refunded. 
5. Submit: Complete and submit your application before the last date. 
The Entrance Test 
Test Format: 
 
Type: Online proctored test (computer-based) 
 
Duration: 2 hours 
 
Total Questions: 100 multiple choice questions 
 
Time: 10:00 AM to 12:00 Noon 

 
Marking: Each question = 1 mark, No negative marking 
What Will Be Tested: 
Part A - Computer Fundamentals (50 questions, 50 marks): 
 
Digital Logic and Boolean Algebra 
 
Computer Organization and Architecture 
 
Programming in C and Data Structures 
 
Algorithms and Problem Solving 
 
Operating Systems 
 
Databases and SQL 
 
Computer Networks 
 
Software Engineering 
Part B - General Knowledge (50 questions, 50 marks): 
 
Mathematics (Sets, Probability, Statistics) 
 
Analytical and Logical Reasoning 
 
General English (Grammar, Vocabulary, Comprehension) 
Qualifying Marks: You need at least 40% in the written test to move forward. 
Selection Process 
Step 1: Written Test 
 
Your performance in the online entrance test is evaluated 
 
Must score at least 40% to qualify 
Step 2: Interview 
 
Only candidates who qualify the written test are called for an interview 
 
Interview is conducted online 
 
Interview carries 100 marks 
Final Selection: 
 
Your merit list rank is based on: Written Test (60% weightage) + Interview (40% 
weightage) 
 
To qualify: You need at least 38 marks in the interview AND be in the top 600 
candidates overall 

 
Final merit list is published on the website 
 
Waitlisted candidates may be called in later rounds if seats become available 
Admission Cancellation 
Your admission can be cancelled if: 
 
You provided false or incomplete information in the application 
 
You fail to submit your degree certiﬁcate by the deadline (31 October 2026) 
 
You don't secure the minimum required marks in your bachelor's degree 
Reservations and Quotas 
BIT Jaipur follows these reservation rules: 
 
SC (Scheduled Caste): 15% seats 
 
ST (Scheduled Tribe): 7.5% seats 
 
OBC-NCL: Reserved seats (certiﬁcate must be issued after 1 April 2026) 
 
PwD (Persons with Disability): 5% seats 
 
EWS (Economically Weaker Section): Up to 10% seats 
 
State Quota: 50% seats for students whose graduation is from Rajasthan 
 
Other States: 50% remaining seats for all other states 
Scholarships 
Eligible SC/ST, OBC-NCL, and PwD students should submit scholarship forms in the 
Scholarship Section by February each year to receive UGC scholarship beneﬁts.

Holistic Learning: Beyond technical skills, the program includes courses in soft

Global Recognition: MCA alumni work in top companies across India and 
abroad.

ABOUT THE PROGRAMME 
The M.Sc. Animation Design Programme at BIT Jaipur Campus was established in 2009, 
building on the success of the B.Sc. Animation & Multimedia course that started in 
2005. The institution has graduated sixteen successful batches of undergraduate 
students, many of whom are working in prestigious animation companies across India 
and abroad. Some graduates have also started their own businesses successfully. 
The programme is designed to provide value addition in Animation Design and opens 
opportunities for specialization in areas such as:

 
Comics and Digital Games 
 
Visual EƯects 
 
Graphics 
 
2D and 3D Digital Art 
 
Film Making 
The program also equips students with the knowledge and technical expertise to start 
their own design and content development centers to become industrial entrepreneurs. 
Infrastructure and Facilities 
The institution has excellent academic and experimental infrastructure including: 
 
Animation labs with professional animation design software tools 
 
1:1 man-machine ratio (one computer per student) 
 
A constantly growing library with animation titles 
 
Spare labs available for extra study sessions 
 
Common Internet lab for student use 
 
Regular visits from eminent animation professionals from the industry who 
conduct lectures and workshops 
 
Involvement in live projects from government and industry to provide real project 
exposure 

The course structure combines both IT-enabled and art-based learning to 
accommodate both technical and creative aspects of animation.

Department Activities and Achievements 
I) BIT Jaipur Signs MoU with Drishti iHub, IIT Jodhpur for Collaboration in Animation and 
Digital Games 
We are pleased to announce that the Department of Animation & Multimedia, BIT Jaipur has recently signed a 
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Drishti iHub, IIT Jodhpur, marking a significant step towards 
academic and industry collaboration in the field of Animation and Digital Games. 
This partnership aims to foster innovation, skill development, and practical exposure for students. Under this 
MoU, there will be opportunities to jointly organize short-term courses, workshops, seminars, and other 
interactive academic activities, providing students with enriched learning experiences and industry-relevant 
knowledge. 
This collaboration not only strengthens our academic network but also opens up new avenues for our students to 
engage with cutting-edge developments in digital media and gaming technologies. 
II) International Academic Collaboration: Columbia University and BIT Join Hands on 
Environmental Animation Projects 
The Department of Animation & Multimedia, BIT Jaipur will soon begin work on two animated short films 
addressing the issue of air pollution, in collaboration with Columbia University. A two-member team from 
Columbia University recently visited the department. During the visit, Professor Pam Litvik, Associate Dean of 
Research Resources at Columbia University, and Professor Pam Factor engaged with the faculty members of the 
Animation & Multimedia Department to discuss potential collaborative projects. Also present during the 
interaction were Dr. Piyush Tewari (Director), Professor Krishna Mohan, and Ms. Radhika Sharma, Director of 
Jeevan Ashram NGO. 
III) Birla Institute of Technology Mesra, Jaipur Collaborates with Polish Foundation for 
Animation and Comics 
BIT Mesra Jaipur Campus, India, has entered into an international collaboration with the Nil Desperandum 
Foundation, Poland, to develop an animation and comics-based project rooted in historical narratives. 
The collaboration was formalized during a recent visit by Monika Kowalecz from the Polish foundation, who 
interacted with Dr. Vibhuti Pandya, Head of the Animation & Multimedia Department, along with faculty 
members and students. 
The project focuses on creatively presenting archival materials and personal diaries from Poland's World War II 
history. It aims to engage younger audiences through digital platforms, including social media, as well as 
through potential comic book publications. 
The Nil Desperandum Foundation brings with it a rich repository of archival resources, particularly stories 
related to the "Good Maharajas" and the Polish refugees who found shelter in India during World War II. 
Special emphasis will be given to the experiences of Polish children who were hosted and protected during that 
period. 
This collaboration is expected to provide students with valuable international exposure while preserving and 
promoting significant historical narratives through the medium of animation and comics. 

Key Project: Maharaja's Children 
The collaboration produced a significant project titled "Maharaja's Children - A Brave Bunch in India," which 
tells the story of one thousand children saved from the hell of World War II. The project is based on true stories 
and has been recognized at various film festivals including Sundance Film Festival and Krakow Film Festival. 
The project showcases archival materials and personal narratives from Poland's World War II history, 
particularly focusing on the experiences of Polish children who were hosted and protected by Indian 
"Maharajas" during World War II. This initiative represents a unique Indo-Polish cultural and historical 
collaboration. 
Summary of International Collaborations 
The Department of Animation & Multimedia at BIT Jaipur has established itself as a hub for international 
academic collaboration, with partnerships focusing on: 
● 
Digital Media and Gaming Technologies - Through partnership with Drishti iHub, IIT Jodhpur 
● 
Environmental Animation and Social Awareness - Through collaboration with Columbia University on 
air pollution awareness projects 
● 
Historical Narratives and Cultural Preservation - Through partnership with Nil Desperandum 
Foundation, Poland, focusing on World War II stories and Polish-Indian heritage 
These collaborations provide students with valuable international exposure, hands-on experience on real-world 
projects, and opportunities to engage with cutting-edge developments in animation, comics, and digital media.

Children" project, and event documentation showing faculty members, international collaborators, and students 
participating in these initiatives]

Rajasthan AVGC-XR Summit (RAS) 2025 
Birla Institute of Technology (BIT) Jaipur Campus, in collaboration with the Rising 
AVGC-XR and Media Association (RAMA), successfully organized the Rajasthan 
AVGC-XR Summit (RAS) 2025 at Birla Auditorium, Jaipur, on 28 October 2025 to 
celebrate International Animation Day. The landmark event brought together industry 
leaders, policymakers, educators, entrepreneurs, creative professionals, and students 
to discuss the future of India's Creative Economy and the rapidly growing AVGC-XR 
sector. 
The summit was organized in alignment with the Rajasthan AVGC-XR Policy 2024 and the 
Atal Innovation Acceleration and Studio Support (AISA) initiative. The event aimed to 
strengthen Rajasthan's position as a leading hub for Animation, Visual EƯects, Gaming, 
Comics, and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) by promoting innovation, skill development, 
entrepreneurship, and industry collaboration. 
The Rising AVGC-XR and Media Association (RAMA) envisioned the summit as a platform 
to connect talent, industry, academia, and government stakeholders while showcasing 
Rajasthan's growing capabilities in the creative technology sector. 
India's Growing Creative Economy 
India's creative economy is rapidly emerging as an important contributor to national 
development and is expected to contribute more than $100 billion to the country's GDP 
by 2030. Supported by initiatives such as the "Create in India" mission and the National 
AVGC-XR Task Force, the sector is creating new opportunities in animation, gaming, 
immersive technologies, digital design, and storytelling. 
With technologies such as Artiﬁcial Intelligence (AI), Extended Reality (XR), and Gaming 
transforming industries including education, entertainment, healthcare, and tourism, 
India is becoming a global centre for creative innovation. Rajasthan is also playing an 
increasingly important role in this transformation. 
Summit Highlights 
The half-day summit, held at Birla Auditorium, Jaipur, brought together more than 1,200 
participants, including policymakers, industry leaders, investors, academicians, 
students, and creative professionals from across the country. 
The summit featured insightful keynote sessions by renowned experts: 
 
Rajat Ojha, CEO of Gamitronics, spoke on "The Future is Real-Time: How XR is 
Reshaping Entertainment and Learning." 
 
Rajiv Chilaka, creator of Chhota Bheem, shared his journey in "Building the 
Billion Animation Brand." 

 
Mahavir Pratap Sharma, Co-founder of Rajasthan Angels, discussed "Investing 
in India's Creative Tech Renaissance." 
 
Ashwin Kumar from Kleem Productions presented insights into the making of 
the successful animated ﬁlm Mahavatar Narsimha. 
 
Rashi Agarwal explored the impact of Generative AI on the future of animation. 
 
Ishan Shukla shared his experiences from independent ﬁlmmaking to working 
on Star Wars: Visions. 
The event also witnessed participation from ten state-level creative industry associations 
representing Telangana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab, Goa, Delhi, 
Gujarat, West Bengal, and Kerala, reﬂecting the spirit of national collaboration within 
India's creative ecosystem. 
RAMA Awards 2025 
One of the major attractions of the summit was the presentation of the RAMA Awards, 
which recognized outstanding contributions to India's creative and media technology 
sectors. 
 
RAMA Patron Award was presented to Rajat Ojha for taking Rajasthan's creative 
talent to the global stage. 
 
RAMA Legendary Mentor Award was conferred upon Dr. Vibhuti Pandya in 
recognition of his 25 years of dedicated leadership, teaching excellence, and 
mentorship that has inspired thousands of students in animation, design, and 
creative education. 
 
RAMA Young Achiever Award was awarded to Sonam Shekhawat, a BIT Mesra 
alumna and accomplished screenwriter, for her remarkable contributions to 
global animated storytelling. 
These awards reﬂected RAMA's commitment to celebrating creativity, innovation, and 
mentorship within the AVGC-XR sector. 
Rajasthan CreatoVerse 
The summit also introduced the Rajasthan CreatoVerse, a unique experiential 
showcase that highlighted the creative capabilities of the state. The exhibition featured 
interactive installations, audio-visual experiences, digital artworks, and printed displays 
presented by studios, educational institutions, creative professionals, and RAMA 
members. 
The CreatoVerse successfully demonstrated how art, technology, and storytelling can 
come together to create immersive experiences and inspire future creators. 

  
Launch of RAMA Yatra 
The event concluded with the grand launch of the RAMA Yatra, a statewide outreach and 
mentorship initiative designed to identify, nurture, and empower creative talent across 
Rajasthan. Through workshops, mentoring sessions, and industry engagement, the Yatra 
aims to create a strong talent pipeline for India's growing media and creative technology 
sectors. 
Unveiling of "Rasyo" – Rajasthan's Creative Mascot 
A special highlight of the summit was the unveiling of "Rasyo," Rajasthan's oƯicial 
creative mascot. 
Designed as an AI-powered immersive camel, Rasyo symbolizes the blend of Rajasthan's 
rich cultural heritage and modern technological innovation. The mascot will represent 
Rajasthan's creative identity and serve as the face of future RAMA initiatives, including 
the RAMA Yatra and upcoming creative economy programs. 
Conclusion 
The Rajasthan AVGC-XR Summit (RAS) 2025 was a remarkable success, showcasing 
Rajasthan's growing strength in animation, gaming, visual eƯects, immersive 
technologies, and digital storytelling. Through the collaborative eƯorts of BIT Mesra, 
Jaipur Campus and RAMA, the summit provided a valuable platform for knowledge 
sharing, networking, innovation, and industry-academia collaboration. 
The event reinforced Rajasthan's vision of becoming a leading creative technology 
destination in India and highlighted the importance of nurturing talent, encouraging 
entrepreneurship, and building a sustainable creative ecosystem for the future.

Educational Trip to Udaipur 
An educational excursion to Udaipur was organized by the Animation & Multimedia Department, BIT Jaipur, 
from September 30 to October 2, 2024. A total of 53 students, along with faculty members, participated in this 
immersive trip aimed at enhancing their understanding of art, culture, and heritage through real-world 
experiences. 
The journey began on the night of September 30, with participants traveling in a super luxury AC bus. Upon 
arrival in Udaipur on October 1, the group checked in at MD Vailly Red Tulip Resort near Badi Lake. Over two 
days, students explored various cultural and artistic landmarks including Fateh Sagar Lake, Saheliyon ki Bari, 
City Palace, Gangour Ghat, and prominent art galleries. These visits provided valuable insights into traditional 
and contemporary art forms, especially miniature paintings and murals depicting mythological themes. 
Day two featured visits to Badi Lake, Bougainvillea Art Gallery, and Sajjangarh Fort. A highlight was attending 
the painting exhibition "My Own Garden" at Takhman 28, where students interacted with celebrated artists such 
as Prof. Vidyasagar Upadhyaya and Sri Lankan artist Chaminda Gamage. The trip concluded with dinner at 
Dhabalogy and a cultural exhibition before returning to Jaipur on October 3. 
Overall, the trip offered a rich learning experience, blending academic enrichment with cultural exposure, and 
significantly contributed to the creative development of the students.

during the Udaipur excursion]

Coordinator: Dr. Vibhuti Pandya, In-charge A&M Dept. BIT Jaipur 
In an exciting story of India and France sharing their cultures, a comic book called "Chai Pe Croissant" was 
released at a special event in the Sawai Man Singh Museum inside the beautiful City Palace of Jaipur. Students 
from the Animation & Multimedia Department at the Jaipur Campus of Birla Institute of Technology Mesra

faculty members from France at the event. This special day showed how two different cultures can come

City Palace, Jaipur, and Dr. Peeyush Tewari, Director of BIT Jaipur. It was designed and executed by Dr. 
Vibhuti Pandya, In-charge of the Animation & Multimedia Department at BIT Jaipur, along with faculty 
members & students. This comic book can be presented as a gift to the President of France, Mr. Emmanuel 
Macron, during his upcoming visit to Jaipur with our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi.

Department of Animation and Multimedia 
Overview 
Established in 2005, the Department of Animation & Multimedia at Birla Institute of Technology (BIT), Mesra 
– Off-Campus Jaipur, is among India's top animation institutes funded by UGC, the Government of India. The 
department emphasizes on AVGC (Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming & Comics). With globalization 
reshaping the film, television, and digital entertainment industry, the demand for skilled professionals in 
animation, VFX, and digital storytelling is higher than ever. At BIT Jaipur, we bridge the gap between art and 
technology, providing students with a world-class curriculum covering 2D & 3D animation, multimedia 
applications, and digital design. 
Programmes 
We offer industry-oriented programs that cater to different career aspirations in the field of animation and 
multimedia: 
Undergraduate Programs 
● 
B.Sc. (Hons.) in Animation & Multimedia (3 / 4 Years) – NEP 2020 
● 
B.Sc. (Hons.) in Visual Communication (3 / 4 Years) – NEP 2020 
This program follows the NEP 2020 guidelines and includes an exit option after 3 years, allowing students to 
graduate with a bachelor's degree. 
Postgraduate Program 
● 
M.Sc. Animation Design (2 Years) 
Our curriculum integrates theory, practical applications, and real-world projects, ensuring students gain hands-
on experience and creative excellence. 
Infrastructural Facilities 
The Department is equipped with a state-of-the-art computer laboratory, featuring over 40+ high-performance 
systems from brands such as iMac, Dell, and HP powered by Intel Core i7 processors to ensure seamless 
performance for graphic-intensive tasks. To provide students with hands-on practical experience, the labs are 
equipped with the latest versions of industry-standard software and tools relevant to animation, multimedia 
design, and digital content creation. 
The software suite includes tools for: 
● 
2D & 3D Animation: Adobe Animate, Autodesk Maya, Blender 
● 
Graphic Design: Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator 
● 
Video Editing & VFX: Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects 
● 
Sound Editing: Adobe Audition, Audacity 
● 
Web Design & Development: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, WordPress, Adobe Dreamweaver 
● 
Multimedia Authoring: Adobe Flash, Unity (for interactive media and gaming) 
This comprehensive infrastructure enables students to work on real-world projects, develop professional 
portfolios, and gain the practical skills necessary for a successful career in the animation and multimedia 
industry.

Title of the invention: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY: CLOUD COMPUTING ADOPTION, IT MANAGEMENT 
STRATEGIES, AND ORGANIZATIONAL IMPLICATIONS 
Abstract: The present invention relates to a system and method for intelligent cloud computing adoption 
and IT management, leveraging artificial intelligence (AI), predictive analytics, and automation to optimize 
cloud migration, resource allocation, security, and governance. The system comprises an AI-powered 
cloud adoption engine that assesses an enterprise's IT infrastructure to generate an optimized cloud 
deployment strategy, an automated IT resource management module for dynamic scaling, a security and 
compliance module for AI-based threat detection and regulatory adherence, and a business impact 
assessment tool for evaluating financial and operational implications. An interactive cloud monitoring 
dashboard provides real-time insights, security alerts, and cost analytics, ensuring seamless cloud 
adoption and management while minimizing operational risks and optimizing performance.

Abstract: Disclosed herein is a system and method for decentralized IoT device authentication and data 
validation using blockchain and artificial intelligence (100) comprises a plurality of IoT devices (102) 
configured to generate device-specific identification data and operational data. The system also includes 
a blockchain network (104) comprising a distributed ledger stored across a plurality of blockchain nodes. 
The system also includes an artificial intelligence (AI) module (106) configured to analyze operational data 
to detect anomalies, inconsistencies, or patterns indicative of unauthorized device access or data 
tampering. The system also includes a smart contract engine (108) configured to automatically trigger 
authentication processes based on said authentication scores. The system also includes a communication 
interface (110) configured to enable secure, encrypted transmission of data between IoT devices, 
blockchain network, and AI module.

Dr. Abhishek Tiwari is an Assistant Professor in Computer Science with over a decade of academic, 
teaching, and research experience, specializing in Artificial Intelligence for Healthcare. He currently serves 
at Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, and has previously held faculty positions at Bennett University 
(Times of India Group), Galgotias Educational Institutions, ABES Engineering College, and ITM University. 
He earned his Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence (HCL 
Group R&D), where his research focused on deep learning–based frameworks for sparse diffusion MRI 
analysis. His work addresses clinically relevant challenges in neuroimaging, particularly early diagnosis of 
neurological and psychiatric disorders. 
Dr. Tiwari has published extensively in Q1 SCI journals and top-tier international conferences (Core Rank 
A/A*), including ICCV, ACML, ICPR, and WACV. He is the inventor of an Indian utility patent in AI-driven 
diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder and the author of an international research monograph on 
diffusion MRI. His professional contributions span teaching, mentoring, funded research, patents, and 
global academic collaborations, with a strong commitment to advancing explainable, ethical, and energy-
efficient AI for real-world healthcare impact.

Department of Computer Science and Engineering 
Overview 
The Department of Computer Science at BIT's Jaipur campus is well abreast of the latest developments in the area of 
IT, software development and hardware design and regularly incorporates the same in its academic programmes. The 
thrust areas for the department at present are the emerging fields of soft computing and applications, Artificial 
Intelligence, optimisation and control-based software, mobile application development, high-level multilingual 
search, Data mining, Big Data Applications, Cognitive Science & social networking, etc. The objective of various 
courses is to impart quality education through a curriculum in accordance with the challenging software needs of the 
industry and to provide excellent technical knowledge and computing skills. With an excellent knowledge base and 
technical competence, the department's students have an impressive placement record. Many graduates choose to join 
some of the best institutions of higher learning around the world, whereas many of them join the reputed IT and 
leading software industries, such as Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, Samsung, Verizon, D etc. 
Infrastructural Facilities 
The department has eight high-tech computer laboratories with over 400 machines of IBM, Compaq, Dell and HP 
connected to the latest state-of-the-art servers and Core i7/i5 desktops. With the objective of giving the students 
adequate practical exposure, the department has the latest versions of all required software. The software available for 
Computer Science courses are NetSim, ESET, MS-Office, Windows Server 2012, Rational Rose, Oracle, Auto Cad, 
MATLAB, C, C++, Java, Python, and PHP.

We are proud to share that a team of our students from BIT Mesra, Jaipur Campus—Sahil Arora, Rashmi Kumari,

Hackathon, held during Digifest Rajasthan 2026 on 5–6 January 2026 in Jaipur. 
The state-level hackathon was organised by the Government of Rajasthan (GoR) in association with TiE Global and 
witnessed participation from hundreds of teams across Rajasthan, making the competition extremely intense and 
prestigious. 
The winning team was awarded a cash prize of ₹1,50,000 (One Lakh Fifty Thousand Rupees) for developing an AI-
enabled, geo-verified mobile solution designed for real-time field surveys and intelligent anomaly detection—a 
solution with strong potential for use in governance, infrastructure monitoring, and public service delivery. 
Congratulations to the entire team on this outstanding success!

Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering

Overview 
The Department of Electrical & Electronics Engineering is dedicated to the current needs of industry with 
the flexibility to tune its programmes according to different requirements. Application of new technology 
in various fields is one of the main focuses in the activities of the department. Department of EEE, BIT 
Mesra, has received grants amounting to Rs. 4.5 Crore in recent past from ERLDC (Grid Controller of India), 
SERB-DST, ICMR, CCL, UGC, DST, AICTE etc. to strengthen the research facility of the department. The 
department involves with different industries like TATA Motors, Orient Electric Ltd. Larsen & Toubro 
Technology Services (LTTS) for knowledge sharing and problem solving. MoUs have recently been signed 
with ERLDC, TATA Motors, LTTS, CIL, University of Windsor, Canada. 
Infrastructural Facilities 
The Department has excellent lab infrastructure in the area of Control System & Instrumentation, Power 
Electronics, Power Systems, Electrical Machines, Transmission & Distribution of Electrical Power, Switch 
Gear and Protection, Basic Electronics, Integrated Electronics, DSP and Microprocessor. 
The department is equipped with MATLAB, MULTISIM, LabView with ELVIS, My Power, ETAP, Ansys 
Electromagnetic Suite, Infoletica MagNet 2D etc. 
Key Research Area of Interest 
Optimized Power Transmission System, Smart Grid, Solar Energy Systems, Mechatronics, Miniaturization 
and Automation, Computerized Network, etc. Programmes.

Development of a Microcontroller Based Technology of a Pressure Sensitive Bed for 
Immovable Patients to Reduce the Risk of Bed Sore 
Sanctioned by: Indian Council of Medical Research, New Delhi 
Amount Sanctioned: Rs. 9,65,941/- 
Aim 
The aim was to design and develop a bed in which surface pressure of different parts will change automatically after 
a predetermined time. This was done by inflation and deflation action at different pressure by air supply unit 
(Compressor/ Vacuum pumps) whose motors are controlled through a programmable microcontroller. The segment 
or cell wise pressure was changed through microcontrollers in this innovative technology.

Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering 
BIT Jaipur 
Overview 
Electronics provides basic hardware support to Compute basic control and display systems to all kind of 
instruments and mechanical and electrical machines. It is backbone of the entertainment and utility devices and 
gadgets. When it combines with communication, it brings miracle technologies in wireline and wireless 
connectivity and networking like; Satellite Communication, Mobile Communication, Optical Communication, 
Broad Band SDH & ADSL, Internet and Intranet, Wireless in Local Loop (WLL), Bluetooth, etc. In nutshell, the 
advancement in the Electronics & Communication Engineering has played the vital role in realization of the 
concept of ‘Global Village’. 
Infrastructural Facilities 
The Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering in the institution conforms to the global scenario 
with its knowledge base, experience and infrastructure. It has excellent lab infrastructure in the area of Basic 
Electronics, Control System & Instrumentation, Integrated Electronics, Analog & Digital Circuits, Semiconductor 
& Microelectronics, VLSI, DSP, Micro-controller & Microprocessor, Analog & Digital Communication, Optical 
Communication, Microwaves and Antenna. The department has well equipped simulation lab having software 
simulation tools like CADENCE, MATLAB, MULTISIM, COMSIM, Code Composure Studio for DSP, Lab 
view with ELVIS Hardware, HFSS Antenna Simulator, Xilinx's ISE Foundation for VLSI design, System Vue, 
Open IT Guru, etc. 
Programmes 
B.Tech. in Electronics and Communication Engineering (4 years course) 
Key Research Area of Interest 
Communication Systems & Networks, Software Defined Radio, Microelectronics & VLSI, Microwave & 
Milimeter Wave Circuits, Optical Networks & Photonics, Microstrip Antennas, Control & Automation, Signal 
Processing, Virtual Reality, etc.

PROFESSIONAL BACKGROUND 
Dr. Puneet Sharma is an Assistant Professor in Electronics and Communication Engineering at Birla 
Institute of Technology, Mesra – Jaipur Campus, where he has been serving since June 2017. He brings 
over fourteen years of academic, research, and administrative experience, with a strong focus on 
teaching, applied research, and technology development. 
He received his B.E. in Electronics Engineering from the University of Rajasthan (2009), followed by an 
M.Tech. from MNIT Jaipur (2015). He earned his Ph.D. from MNIT Jaipur, with his doctoral research 
focused on "Synthesis and Characterisation of Polymer-Based Sensors for Electronic Applications." His 
research work emphasizes material innovation, sensor design, and real-world applicability. 
Dr. Sharma's research contributions span flexible and wearable sensors, polymer nanocomposites, 
nanomaterial-based electrodes, biomedical instrumentation, and embedded sensor systems. He has 
actively worked on MWCNT-, graphene-, and PDMS-based flexible sensors, particularly for biomedical and 
healthcare monitoring applications. His work has resulted in multiple journal publications, conference 
papers, and granted patents, including a granted Indian patent (2025) on a flexible strain sensor for 
respiration rate detection, reflecting the translational and application-driven nature of his research. 
In addition to academic research, Dr. Sharma has been deeply involved in industry-oriented and 
innovation-driven activities. He has coordinated student projects, internships, and startup initiatives, and 
has actively contributed to the development of incubation and entrepreneurship ecosystems at the 
institutional level. His engagement includes mentoring student startups, coordinating industry 
collaborations, and supporting technology commercialization efforts. 
Dr. Sharma has also held several key administrative and leadership roles, including Technical Manager of 
an NABL-accredited calibration laboratory, Training and Internship Coordinator, Project Coordinator for 
undergraduate students, Startup Cell Coordinator, and mentor to multiple technical and innovation clubs. 
Through these roles, he has contributed to curriculum enrichment, laboratory development, quality 
assurance, and student skill development. 

He actively participates in national and international research collaborations, workshops, and faculty 
development programs, and has delivered expert talks at reputed institutions. His current interests 
include expanding international collaborations, particularly in Indo-European research frameworks, and 
advancing industry-relevant, patent-driven, and socially impactful technologies.

Programme Outcomes 
Engineering Graduates will be able to: 
1. 
Engineering knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and 
an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems. 
2. 
Problem analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering 
problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and 
engineering sciences. 
3. 
Design/development of solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design 
system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the 
public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations. 
4. 
Conduct investigations of complex problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods 
including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to 
provide valid conclusions. 
5. 
Modern tool usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern 
engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an 
understanding of the limitations. 
6. 
The engineer and society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, 
health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional 
engineering practice. 
7. 
Environment and sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in 
societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable 
development. 
8. 
Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the 
engineering practice. 
9. 
Individual and team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse 
teams, and in multidisciplinary settings. 
10. Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering 
community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and 
design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions. 
11. Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and 
management principles and apply these to one's own work, as a member and leader in a team, to 
manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

Overview 
The Department of Management was established with the aim of serving the growing need for qualified 
professionals who could harness the resources of the country to achieve its development goals. The department has 
continuously strived to achieve this aim by maintaining the highest standards in the Under Graduate (BBA). 
The vision of the department today is to be recognized as a frontrunner in Management education in the country in 
consonance with the social, economic and ecological environment while striving to contribute to nation building 
through excellence in research and development activities. 
The department follows the philosophy of Outcome Based Education. Therefore, the teaching-learning process is 
student centric. The pedagogy is practical, hands on and real time. Case studies, Problem Solving Exercises, Role-
Plays, Management Games and Presentations are extensively used. The curriculum is planned to facilitate learning 
in theory and practice of all aspects of the discipline of management ensuring the achievement of predefined 
learning outcomes.

BBA Programme 
The Department of Management offers: 
BBA Programme (as per NEP 2020 Guidelines) 
Need and Aim of the BBA Programme 
The mission of the BBA program is to equip the students with theoretical concepts, good communication skills 
and adequate business knowledge. The program also imparts requisite creative and ethical competency through 
intensive training for developing overall personality, thereby inculcating self-confidence and team spirit of the 
student. The training pedagogy comprises Case Analysis Presentations, Group Discussions, Problem Solving 
Techniques appraising the real-life business problems with analytical ability and thus the students will be prepared 
to meet the expectations of the industry under fast changing virtual business environment. The graduates turn 
out to be well versed to opt for higher education or entry level managerial assignments. The former students of 
the BBA program of our institute are well placed in leading organizations in India and abroad, thereby adding 
laurels to their alma mater. 
Programme Structure and Duration 
The 4 years full time BBA program with multiple EXIT options adopts a Semester system comprising two semesters 
(Monsoon and Spring) in an academic year. The Monsoon semester is held during July to December while the 
Winter Semester is from January to May, with sixteen weeks of class in each semester. The program follows a 
combination of Progressive and End Semester Evaluation of student performance. 
Course Structure 
The course structure includes Ability Enhancement Courses, Skill-Enhancement Courses, Value-Added Courses, 
Multidisciplinary Courses, and Core Management Courses, along with courses in Functional Electives in the 
following areas: 
• Finance 
• Marketing 
• Human Resources 
• Information Technology 
• Digital Marketing 
• Business Analytics

PROFESSIONAL BACKGROUND 
Dr. Prince Kumar Maurya is an academician and researcher in the field of Finance, currently serving as an 
Assistant Professor in the Department of Management at Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra. He holds a 
Ph.D. in Finance from the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology (an Institution of National 
Importance), where his doctoral research focused on investor sentiment, volatility connectedness, and 
hedging opportunities in financial markets. He also completed his MBA in Finance and Marketing from 
Aligarh Muslim University and a B.Sc. (Hons.) in Electronics from the University of Delhi. 
Dr. Maurya brings a blend of academic and industry experience, having previously served as an Assistant 
Professor at Manav Rachna International Institute of Research and Studies and worked as an Assistant 
Project Coordinator in the infrastructure sector. His teaching portfolio includes Financial Management, 
Corporate Finance, Investment Analysis and Portfolio Management, Financial Derivatives, and Cost & 
Management Accounting. 
His research contributions are published in reputable international journals indexed in Scopus and ABDC,

International Conference on Sustainability: Research, Education and Practice (SREP-2022) 
Dates: 30-31 May 2022 
Venue / Host: Department of Management, BIT Mesra, Jaipur, Lalpur, Noida, Patna 
The Government of India launched the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav to honour and celebrate 75 years of progressive India and 
the magnificent history of its people, culture, and achievements. The Department of Management of BIT Mesra, Jaipur, 
Lalpur, Noida, and Patna hosted the two-day International Conference on Sustainability: Research, Education and Practice on 
30-31 May, 2022, as part of this celebration. 
The conference provided a platform for deliberations on sustainability as a form of celebration of the progress of the country. 
In the contemporary world, sustainability has emerged as an important area of focus in research, education, and practice — 
a paradigm concerned about the future in which environmental, societal, and economic considerations are balanced in the 
pursuit of improved quality of life. 
The conference had three main tracks: Sustainability and Human Resource Management; Sustainability in Marketing Practices 
and Research; and Sustainability in Public Services and General Management. Seventy-seven research papers were presented 
under the different tracks over the two-day international conference, covering sustainability across the various identified 
areas. 
The conference featured distinguished expert speakers from academia and industry who delivered Plenary Sessions during 
the course of the event. 
Plenary Session Speakers: 
• Mr. Pankaj Sinha, Managing Director, Coca Cola Sri Lanka and Maldives. 
• Prof. Alok Chaturvedi, Director, Institute for Social Empowerment through Entrepreneurship & Knowledge, Krannert 
School of Business, Purdue University — Topic: "Road to Prosperity in Harmony with People and Planet." 
• Prof. Bhimaraya Metri, Director, IIM Nagpur. 
• Prof. Rama Seth, Visiting Professor, Copenhagen Business School. 
The conference aimed to bring together researchers, practitioners, educators, and students to exchange ideas on the pillars 
of sustainability. It was conceptualized to provide a platform to share cutting-edge research in the field, featuring a galaxy of 
speakers sharing their thoughts on contemporary management issues and sustainability issues.

the magnificent history of its people, culture, and achievements. The Department of Management of BIT Mesra, Jaipur, 
Lalpur, Noida, and Patna hosted the two-day International Conference on Sustainability: Research, Education and Practice on 
30-31 May, 2022, as part of this celebration. 
This conference provided a platform for deliberations on sustainability as a form of celebration of the progress of the country. 
In the contemporary world, sustainability has emerged as an important area of focus in research, education, and practice — 
a paradigm concerned about the future in which environmental, societal, and economic considerations are balanced in the 
pursuit of improved quality of life. 
The conference had three main tracks: Sustainability and Human Resource Management, Sustainability in Marketing Practices 
and Research, and Sustainability in Public Services and General Management. Seventy-seven research papers were presented 
under the different tracks over the two-day conference, covering sustainability across the various identified areas. The 
conference featured distinguished expert speakers from academia and industry who delivered four plenary sessions during 
the course of the event. It aimed to bring together researchers, practitioners, educators, and students to exchange ideas on 
the pillars of sustainability, providing a platform to share cutting-edge research and hear from a galaxy of speakers on 
contemporary management and sustainability issues.

Department of Sciences 
BIT Jaipur 
Overview 
The Department of Sciences of BIT Mesra, Off-Campus Jaipur is an integral part of the Institute. It combines all the 
important streams of Science i.e. Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry, Environmental Science amd Biological Science 
etc. The department supports in teaching of UG & PG courses of Engineering and Management. The department is 
extensively engaged in basic and applied research in Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry & Biological 
Sciences/Biotechnology in various specializations. 
Vision of the Department 
The vision of the department is to achieve excellence in Basic and Applied Sciences required for undergraduate 
courses in Engineering and Management discipline. The department vision also focus to carryout research activities 
on new and emerging technologies for development of new knowledge and benefit of society. 
Mission of the Department 
• 
To train the students to be lifelong learners who will contribute to the creation of new knowledge, new 
technology, and innovation through excellence in research in emerging areas. 
• 
To educate students to be the future leaders in areas of science, technology, industry, entrepreneurship and 
other professions to succeed in a globally competitive environment. 
• 
To create national and international collaborations for research engagement in strategic areas of research. 
• 
To carryout basic and applied research in various disciplines of Science. 
• 
To carryout Scientific activities involving different levels of students and teachers. 
Key Research Area 
Physics: Plasma Physics, Industrial Plasma Applications, Plasma-Based Surface Modification, Material Science, 
Microstrip Patch Antennas and RF Systems 
Mathematics: Heat and Mass Transfer in Boundary layer flows, Fluid Dynamics 
Chemistry: Ground Water Analysis and Environmental Pollution, Environmental Science & Biological Science, 
Industrial Water Pollution, Soil and Invironmental Studies 
Biological Sciences: Biotechnology and Computational Biology

Research Areas 
BIT Jaipur 
The department of sciences is engaged in the following focused research areas. 
Physics Research Areas 
• 
Plasma Science and Technology: Atmospheric pressure glow discharge, DBD sources, Plasma medicine, 
Plasma nitriding, Impurity transport in tokamak plasma. 
• 
Material Science & Technology: Plasma based material treatment, Materials testing and Analysis. 
• 
Micro-strip Antenna designs: Microstrip Antennas and Arrays, Broadband, Ultra-Wideband, Super Ultra-
Wideband Antennas and RF communication technology. 
Chemistry Research Areas 
• 
Ground Water Analysis and Environmental Pollution 
• 
Industrial Water Pollution, Soil and Environmental Studies 
• 
Environmental and Biological Sciences 
Mathematics Research Areas 
• 
Heat and Mass Transfer in Boundary Layer Flows 
• 
Fluid Dynamics

BIT Jaipur Placement Process 
The placement process at BIT Jaipur operates under the centralized Training and 
Placement (T&P) division of BIT Jaipur. Students register on the BIT Jaipur Placement 
Portal, attend pre-placement talks, participate in recruitment drives, and receive oƯers 
through a structured, tier-based system. 
1. Registration & Proﬁle Building 
 
Portal Activation: Students activate their account on the BIT Placement Portal 
using their Roll Number and ERP credentials. 
 
Resume & Guidelines: Students must accept the institute's placement policy, 
ﬁll out their proﬁle details, and upload necessary document proofs for faculty 
veriﬁcation. 
2. Company Announcement & Registration 
 
Job Publication: Companies share their Job Application Form (JAF), which 
includes eligibility criteria, job descriptions, pay, and rewards. 
 
Application: Eligible and interested students register for speciﬁc company 
drives through the T&P portal. 
3. Recruitment Drives & Selection 
 
Process Location: Students from the Jaipur extension centre sit for Mass 
Recruiters directly, while some Tier-1 and speciﬁc core companies may require 
students to participate in drives alongside the main Mesra campus students. 
 
Testing Formats: The selection process typically involves online assessments 
(Aptitude, Coding, Technical), Group Discussions (GDs), and Personal Interviews 
(PI). 
4. OƯer Policy & Norms 
 
Tier and Dream OƯers: Placed students in IT services or core companies may 
not be allowed to sit for further drives unless selected for "Dream Recruiters" at

BIT Jaipur Fee Refund and Withdrawal Policy - 2026-27 
Who Does This Apply To? 
This policy is for newly admitted students in undergraduate (UG), postgraduate (PG), 
and Ph.D. programs at BIT Mesra and its Extension Centers for the 2026-27 academic 
year. 
Important: This policy does NOT apply to NRI students, OCI students, or Foreign 
National (FN) students. 
 
What Happens When You Withdraw? 
You can get a refund of your fees if you decide to leave your program after admission. 
The amount you get back depends on when you withdraw. 
There are two diƯerent scenarios based on when you took admission - before classes 
started or after classes started. 
 
SCENARIO 1: You Got Admission BEFORE Classes Began 
Withdrawal Before Classes Start 
 
What you get: Your full fee back minus Rs. 10,000 as a processing charge 
 
Example: If you paid Rs. 1,00,000 and withdraw before day 1 of class, you get Rs. 
90,000 back 
Withdrawal Between Day 1 and Day 7 (After Classes Start) 
 
Condition: There must be another round of admissions coming up where your 
seat can be ﬁlled 
 
What you get: 80% of the fees you paid at the time of admission 
 
Important: The refund amount is rounded up to the nearest Rs. 100 
 
Example: If you paid Rs. 1,00,000, you get 80,000. If the 80% comes to Rs. 
80,050, it becomes Rs. 80,100 
Withdrawal After 7 Working Days From Class Start 
 
What you get: 60% of the fees you paid at the time of admission 
 
Rounding: Again, rounded up to the nearest Rs. 100 
 
Example: If you paid Rs. 1,00,000, you get Rs. 60,000 back 

Withdrawal After Admission Process Is Closed 
 
What you get: Only your caution money back (no other refund) 
 
Caution money: This is the security deposit you gave, typically a small amount 
 
SCENARIO 2: You Got Admission AFTER Classes Already Started 
Withdrawal Within 7 Working Days of Your Admission 
 
Condition: There must be another round of admissions coming up where your 
seat can be ﬁlled 
 
What you get: 80% of the fees you paid at the time of admission 
 
Rounding: Rounded up to the nearest Rs. 100 
Withdrawal After 7 Working Days From Your Admission Date 
 
What you get: 60% of the fees you paid at the time of admission 
 
Rounding: Rounded up to the nearest Rs. 100 
Withdrawal After Admission Process Is Closed 
 
What you get: Only your caution money back 
 
Important Rules You Must Follow 
You Must Apply for the Refund 
 
You cannot just leave and expect money back automatically 
 
You must submit a formal application to withdraw 
 
In your application, you must explain speciﬁc reasons why you are permanently 
leaving the program 
 
The refund will be processed "in due course of time" - meaning it may take some 
time 
When Will You Get Your Money? 
 
After your application is approved 
 
The exact timeline is not speciﬁed, so it could be weeks or months 
 
You should follow up with the administration oƯice 
How Amounts Are Rounded 

 
All refund amounts are rounded up to the next Rs. 100 
 
For example: Rs. 80,050 becomes Rs. 80,100; Rs. 60,001 becomes Rs. 60,100 
 
Special Situations 
Situation 1: You Change Your Center or Program (Same Admission Round) 
If you want to upgrade from one extension center to another center, or from one 
program to another program in the same admission process: 
 
Processing charge: Rs. 1,000 only 
 
What happens to your fees: The balance from your previous program is 
adjusted in your 2nd semester fees of the new program 
Example: You paid Rs. 50,000 for Program A and then switch to Program B (which costs 
Rs. 60,000). Your Rs. 50,000 (minus Rs. 1,000 processing charge) = Rs. 49,000 is 
adjusted toward your 2nd semester of Program B. 
Situation 2: You Got Admission Through Two DiƯerent Admission Processes 
This means you got selected in one admission process, then later got selected again in 
a completely diƯerent admission process (not an upgrade). 
What happens: 
1. You must pay the full fees of your new program - no discount 
2. The fees you paid toward your ﬁrst program are adjusted in your 2nd semester 
fees of the new program 
3. But Rs. 1,000 processing charge is still deducted from your ﬁrst program fees 
4. You must withdraw from your ﬁrst program through the ERP Portal immediately 
after taking admission in the new program 
5. After the admission closure is announced, you must apply separately to the 
Admission OƯice for the fee adjustment 
Example: 
 
Program A costs Rs. 50,000 (you paid) 
 
Program B costs Rs. 60,000 (you get selected later) 
 
You pay full Rs. 60,000 for Program B 
 
In 2nd semester of Program B, Rs. 50,000 - Rs. 1,000 = Rs. 49,000 is adjusted 
from your semester fees 

 
You use the ERP Portal to oƯicially withdraw from Program A

BIT Mesra GP Birla Scholarship Guidelines - Complete Details 
What Is This Scholarship? 
The GP Birla Scholarship is a ﬁnancial aid program started by BIT Mesra to help 
deserving students. It has been running for over six decades and aims to: 
 
Reward students with excellent academic performance 
 
Support students who are economically and socially challenged 
 
Help promising students from poorer ﬁnancial backgrounds 
Valid From: Spring 2024 onwards 
 
Who Can Apply? 
Basic Eligibility 
You can apply for GP Birla Scholarship if: 
✓ You are an undergraduate student in a 4-year or 5-year program 
✓ You were admitted through JEE (Main) or equivalent entrance exam 
✓ You study at BIT Mesra main campus or any of its extension centers 
✗ Postgraduate (PG) and Ph.D. students cannot apply - this is only for undergraduate 
students 
 
Four Types of Scholarships Available 
There are 4 diƯerent scholarship categories. You can qualify for only ONE scholarship at 
a time. 
 
SCHOLARSHIP TYPE 1: Merit-Based Scholarship 
What Is It? 
This scholarship rewards students based on their JEE (Main) exam rank and later, their 
academic performance. 
Amount of Scholarship 
The scholarship is given based on your JEE rank: 

JEE Rank
Scholarship Amount Number of Students
Rank 1 to 1,000
100% of tuition fee
15 students
Rank 1,001 to 2,500 75% of tuition fee
(included in 15)
Rank 2,501 to 5,000 50% of tuition fee
(included in 15)
Important: Only 15 total students get merit scholarship, which includes 10 boys and 5 
girls exclusively. 
How It Works - First Semester (1st Sem) 
 
Your scholarship is based on your JEE (Main) rank 
 
Applied only in your 1st semester 
 
No GPA requirement - just your rank determines it 
How It Works - From Second Semester Onwards (2nd Sem+) 
After 1st semester, the scholarship is given based on your academic performance 
(GPA): 
 
You need to score more than 9.00 GPA in the previous semester 
 
You must have zero backlog courses (no failed or incomplete courses) 
 
15 students who meet this criteria get 100% tuition fee scholarship 
 
This includes 10 boys and 5 girls exclusively 
Important Conditions for Merit Scholarship 
✓ Applied from 2nd semester based on previous semester GPA 
✓ Does NOT apply to students in their ﬁnal semester (graduating students) 
✓ You must have no disciplinary punishment or black dots on your record 
✓ Open to all students - no restrictions on category, caste, or economic background 
 
SCHOLARSHIP TYPE 2: Merit-cum-Means (Economically Weaker Section) 
Who Is This For? 
This is for students from the EWS (Economically Weaker Section) category who have 
both good academics AND ﬁnancial need. 
Eligibility Requirements 

You must meet ALL of these: 
1. Student Type: Undergraduate student in 4/5 year program 
2. Admission: Must be admitted through JEE (Main) or equivalent exam 
3. Category: Must belong to EWS category 
4. Academics: GPA of 8.00 or higher in the previous semester 
5. No Backlogs: Must have zero backlog courses 
6. Family Income: Parents' annual income from all sources must be ≤ 8 lakhs 
Scholarship Amount 
25 students in each category: 
Category A: Income ≤ 4 lakhs 
 
Get 100% tuition fee scholarship 
 
Total of 25 students 
Category B: Income 4 to 8 lakhs 
 
Get 50% tuition fee scholarship 
 
Total of 25 students 
Important Conditions 
✓ Applied from 2nd semester onwards 
✓ Based on previous semester GPA and current family income 
✓ Does NOT apply to graduating students (ﬁnal semester) 
✓ Must have no disciplinary punishment or black dots 
✓ Note: If more than 25 students qualify in a category, the committee can adjust the 
scholarship percentage 
✓ Preference given to students admitted under EWS category 
 
SCHOLARSHIP TYPE 3: Economically and Socially Challenged Students (ESCS) 
Who Is This For? 
This is for students from reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/EBC/NCL) who have 
ﬁnancial need. 
Eligibility Requirements 

You must meet ALL of these: 
1. Student Type: Undergraduate student in 4/5 year program 
2. Admission: Must be admitted through JEE (Main) or equivalent exam 
3. Category: Must belong to SC/ST/OBC/EBC/NCL category 
4. Academics: GPA of 6.50 or higher in the previous semester 
5. Backlogs Allowed: You can have maximum 1 backlog course in the previous 
semester 
6. Family Income: Parents' annual income from all sources must be ≤ 8 lakhs 
7. Income Certiﬁcate: Must provide an oƯicial income certiﬁcate issued by a 
Gazetted OƯicer (CO/SDO/Tehsildar rank or higher) 
Scholarship Amount 
100 students will receive 100% tuition fee scholarship 
This is the highest number of students supported among all categories. 
Important Conditions 
✓ Applied from 2nd semester onwards 
✓ Based on previous semester GPA and family income 
✓ Does NOT apply to graduating students (ﬁnal semester) 
✓ Must have no disciplinary punishment or black dots 
✓ Lower GPA requirement than EWS: You only need 6.50 GPA instead of 8.00 
✓ One backlog allowed: Unlike other categories, you can have 1 failed/incomplete 
course 
 
SCHOLARSHIP TYPE 4: Program Topper Prize 
What Is It? 
This is a cash prize awarded to the student who gets the highest marks in their branch in 
each semester. 
Who Can Get It? 
Top student in each branch/program in a given semester. 
Prize Amount 

Rs. 15,000 per student 
Maximum 60 prizes awarded per semester (so up to 60 toppers get this prize) 
Eligibility 
1. You must be the topper (highest GPA) in your branch 
2. Undergraduate student in 4/5 year program 
3. Admitted through JEE (Main) or equivalent exam 
4. Open to all students - no category, caste, or economic restrictions 
5. Must have no disciplinary punishment or black dots 
Important Conditions 
✓ Applied from 2nd semester onwards 
✓ Based on previous semester GPA (highest GPA in your branch) 
✓ Does NOT apply to graduating students in ﬁnal semester 
✓ One prize per student per semester 
 
Important Terms and Conditions (Applies to ALL Scholarships) 
1. Only for Undergraduate Students 
Only 4/5 year undergraduate programs are eligible. PG and Ph.D. students cannot get 
any of these scholarships. 
2. What the Scholarship Covers 
The scholarship covers tuition fee only - not hostel, mess, books, or other expenses. 
The percentage covered depends on the category and scholarship type. 
3. Budget Information 
 
Total allocated budget: 423.56 lakhs 
 
This is an approximate ﬁgure and can be adjusted based on applications 
received 
4. Not for Graduating Students 
No scholarship is given to students in their ﬁnal semester - the semester when they 
are graduating. 
5. All Campuses Included 

Scholarship is applicable at: 
 
BIT Mesra main campus (Ranchi) 
 
All extension centers of BIT Mesra 
6. Only ONE Scholarship at a Time 
Very Important Rule: You can receive only one scholarship OR one ﬁnancial 
assistantship from BIT at a time 
 
If you get another scholarship from outside sources, you must inform BIT 
 
You need to sign an undertaking saying you haven't received any other 
scholarship 
 
BIT can take disciplinary action if you receive scholarships from multiple sources 
7. Tie-Breaking Rule 
If multiple students have the same GPA, the committee decides who gets the 
scholarship based on criteria they set. 
8. No Disciplinary Issues Allowed 
You cannot get any scholarship if you have: 
 
Any disciplinary punishment on your record 
 
Black dots (marks) on your disciplinary record 
 
Any misconduct history 
Clean record is mandatory. 
9. Institute Can Change Rules 
BIT reserves the right to: 
 
Change the scholarship criteria 
 
Change the percentage of scholarship 
 
Discontinue any scholarship category 
 
Change any rules at any time 
10. Final Decision is Final 
The Institute's decision on all scholarship matters is ﬁnal and binding - you cannot 
appeal. 
 

How to Apply - Selection Procedure 
Step 1: Know the Application Dates 
 
Two application periods per year: 
o Monsoon (MO) Session - one deadline 
o Spring (SP) Session - one deadline 
 
The exact dates are announced by the OƯice of the Dean (Student AƯairs)

Completed application form 
 
Income certiﬁcate (if applicable for your category) 
o Must be issued by a Gazetted OƯicer not below rank of CO/SDO/Tehsildar

o Required for: EWS, ESCS categories 
 
Academic records (transcripts showing GPA) 
 
Proof of admission through JEE (Main) or equivalent 
Step 3: Submit Your Application 
 
Submit before the last date announced by Dean (Student AƯairs) 
 
Include all required documents 
 
Submit completed application with all copies as prescribed 
Step 4: Processing 
 
Applications are reviewed by GP Birla Scholarship Committee

Committee makes recommendations

Final approval given by Vice-Chancellor

Scholarships for Spring (SP) Session are given based on Monsoon (MO) Session

your scholarship for SP session.

Disciplinary Consequences: Violators face strict punitive action, ranging from 
public apologies and suspension to cancellation of admission and rustication.

Black Dot Policy – BIT Jaipur 
 The Black Dot Policy is a disciplinary system implemented to maintain discipline, 
responsibility, and ethical conduct among students at BIT Jaipur. Black dots may 
be awarded to students found violating the Code of Conduct, institutional 
regulations, hostel rules, or engaging in acts of indiscipline. All black dots are 
cumulative in nature and form part of the student's disciplinary record. 
1. A student awarded one Black Dot shall receive a strict warning from the 
college authorities. 
2. A student awarded two Black Dots shall receive a strict warning and may be 
barred from participating in student activities, clubs, societies, cultural 
events, sports activities, and other extracurricular programs organized by the 
institute. 
3. A student awarded three Black Dots shall receive a strict warning and may 
be debarred from participating in campus placement and recruitment 
activities conducted by the institute. 
4. A student awarded four Black Dots may face a semester back of one to two 
years, in addition to other disciplinary measures deemed appropriate by the 
disciplinary committee. 
5. A student awarded ﬁve Black Dots shall be liable for permanent expulsion 
from BIT Jaipur. 
 The institute reserves the right to inform parents or guardians regarding acts of 
indiscipline and the award of black dots. Depending upon the severity of the 
oƯense, the disciplinary committee may also impose additional penalties such 
as ﬁnes, recovery of damages, suspension from hostel facilities, suspension 
from academic or extracurricular activities, rustication, or expulsion. 
 Serious oƯenses including ragging, physical assault, vandalism, substance 
abuse, cyber misconduct, harassment, possession of prohibited substances, or 
any act that threatens the safety, security, reputation, or functioning of the 
institute may attract immediate disciplinary action irrespective of the number of 
black dots previously awarded. 
 All students are expected to maintain the highest standards of discipline, 
integrity, and conduct and uphold the reputation and values of BIT Jaipur at all 
times.

Name: Dr. Abhijit Mondal 
Department: Chemical Engineering 
Project Title: Design and Development of a Rotating Electrode Membraneless Electrolyzer 
(REME) using Electrodeposited Cobalt–Nickel Catalysts for Scalable Green Hydrogen 
Production. 
Funding Agency: Anusandhan National Research Foundation, Advanced Research Grant 
Sanction Amount: 5131680 
ANRF/ARG/2025/00092/ENS       Dated 13th March 2026 
Tenure: 3 Years 
Abstract: Design and Development of a Rotating Electrode Membraneless Electrolyzer (REME) 
using Electrodeposited Cobalt–Nickel Catalysts for Scalable Green Hydrogen Production. 
This project addresses the urgent need for sustainable energy solutions by focusing on green hydrogen production 
as a clean, zero-carbon fuel. Conventional water electrolysis technologies such as alkaline and polymer electrolyte 
membrane (PEM) systems, are limited by high costs, reliance on expensive membranes and noble metal catalysts, 
and complex system architectures. These challenges hinder large-scale adoption despite the growing global interest 
in hydrogen as a key energy carrier. 
To overcome these limitations, the proposal explores a membraneless electrolyzer (ME) approach, which eliminates 
costly membranes and enables the use of abundant, non-precious materials. However, existing MEs suffer from 
issues such as gas crossover and bubble accumulation, which reduce efficiency and increase energy losses. 
The project introduces an innovative Rotating Electrode Membraneless Electrolyzer (REME) to address these 
challenges. The system employs rotating mesh electrodes that generate centrifugal force to effectively remove gas 
bubbles from electrode surfaces, thereby enhancing mass transfer, increasing active surface area, and reducing 
overpotential. A cylindrical separator is incorporated to further minimize gas crossover between electrodes. 
The REME design utilizes cost-effective materials, including cobalt-deposited nickel mesh as the anode and nickel-
modified stainless steel as the cathode, ensuring both performance and affordability. Powered by solar energy, the 
system aligns with sustainability goals. 
By developing a scalable, low-cost, and efficient membraneless electrolyzer, this project aims to fill a critical 
research gap and contribute to the advancement of green hydrogen technologies and the global transition toward a 
decarbonized energy future.

Mathematics 
Project Title: 
Construction of entanglement witnesses exploiting positive maps 
and their optimization procedures. 
Funding Agency: 
National Board for Higher Mathematics (NBHM), Department of 
Atomic Energy (DAE), Govt. of India 
Sanction Amount: 
Rs. 1959200  
Tenure: 
3 Years 
Abstract: 
Entanglement is one of the central concepts of quantum information theory. Beyond its 
fundamental significance, it plays a crucial operational role in a wide range of quantum 
information–processing tasks, including quantum communication, computation, and 
metrology. Many advantages of quantum technologies over their classical counterparts can 
ultimately be traced back to the presence of entanglement. 
 
From a mathematical point of view, entanglement is defined through a  simple structural 
criterion: a quantum state is entangled if it cannot be written as a convex combination of 
product states. While this definition is conceptually clear, its practical implementation becomes 
extremely challenging as the dimension of the underlying Hilbert space increases. In high-
dimensional or multipartite systems, a full characterization of the state typically requires an 
exponentially large number of parameters, rendering standard entanglement detection methods 
infeasible. Moreover, commonly used criteria such as the positive partial transpose condition 
are no longer sufficient to detect all entangled states in higher dimensions, leading to the 
phenomenon of bound entanglement. 
 
The goal of this project is to address these challenges by designing entanglement witnesses 
tailored for high-dimensional quantum systems. In particular, the project will exploit the theory 
of positive but not completely positive maps, which provides a powerful and systematic 
framework for entanglement detection beyond low-dimensional settings. We further aim to 
develop experimentally accessible and computationally efficient tools for certifying 
entanglement in complex quantum systems. These results are expected to contribute both to 
the theoretical understanding of high-dimensional entanglement and to its practical verification 
in realistic quantum information platforms.

Department: Chemical Engineering 
Project Title: Development of an affordable portable non-invasive Electrochemical Impedimetric 
Biosensor for Rapid detection of Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH) in Resource-constrained areas. 
Funding Agency: Department of Health Research (DHR), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
(MoHFW)) 
Sanction Amount: 38.25 Lakhs 
Fund Utilised.: 20720+45890= 66610 (+864800 indent in process) 
Tenure: 3 Years 
 
Abstract:  
Rapid and affordable screening of Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH) is essential for 
early diagnosis of thyroid disorders, especially in resource-constrained regions where 
laboratory infrastructure and trained personnel are limited. This work presents the 
development of a portable, low-cost, non-invasive electrochemical impedimetric biosensor 
integrated with a smartphone-based readout platform for rapid TSH detection. The 
proposed system employs a nanostructured electrode surface functionalized with TSH-
specific antibodies/aptamer, enabling highly sensitive label-free detection through changes 
in interfacial impedance upon antigen binding. A compact potentiostat module based on 
an optimized transimpedance amplifier, low-noise analog front-end, and wireless 
microcontroller is engineered to perform impedance spectroscopy at multiple frequencies. 
A user-friendly mobile application processes the impedance spectra, extracts features, and 
predicts TSH levels using calibration models, providing results within minutes. The 
biosensor demonstrates excellent reproducibility, high sensitivity in the clinically relevant 
range, and strong correlation with standard laboratory immunoassays. Owing to its low 
fabrication cost, minimal sample requirement, and robust field usability, this portable 
impedimetric biosensing system has strong potential for population-level thyroid 
screening and decentralized endocrine health monitoring in low-resource settings.

Name: Dr. Ela Sinha 
Department: Physics 
Project Title: Hafnium Loaded Proton Conducting Oxide for Direct - Hydrocarbon 
                      Intermediate Temperature Solid Oxide Fuel Cell Application. 
 
Funding Agency: Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) 
Sanction Amount: 45,37,192 (in Rs.) 
Sanction Letter: CRG/2023/008073 Dated 01.05.2024    
Tenure: 3 Years 
Abstract:  
The objective of the research proposal is to develop robust direct- hydrocarbon intermediate temperature 
(400-700oC) fuel cell using proton conducting oxides as a compatible and potential power source which 
eradicates the fuel processor units. Further coupling into the current power grid will upgrade their energy 
conversion efficiency and subsidize toxic effluents. Conventional direct- hydrocarbon solid oxide fuel cell 
(SOFC) with high functional temperature (800 -1000 ℃) uses Ni-YSZ as the anode due to their high catalytic 
and electrophysical response. However, material degradation via coking and Sulphur poisoning of the acidic 
YSZ surface forbids coke migration against carbonaceous fuels. This leads to poor long-term durability of 
the system, and the high operating temperature impose shortcomings upon the compositional stability and 
cell performance. To overcome this limitation, investigators have planned to fabricate Ni- modified hafnium 
based rare earth doped barium cerate proton conducting oxide, as robust anode which will accelerates C—
OH formation due to a basic anodic surface with adequate H2O intake. This as a consequence improves the 
coking tolerance at intermediate temperatures resulting longer durability of the fuel cell. Hafnium based rare 
earth doped barium cerate will be used as electrolyte which have a lot of potential in term of chemical 
inertness, high protonation, hydration thermodynamics and low electron transfer numbers at intermediate 
temperatures (400 – 650 ℃). Meanwhile, Cobalt free, complex oxide based on doped barium ferrite as 
cathode materials which considered to improve the transport property, oxygen reduction kinetics as well as 
chemical stability of the cathode. All ceramics synthesis will be carried out via solid state reaction route. 
The detailed structural, chemical, thermal and electrical properties of the materials shall be carried out to 
understand their temperature dependent response under different hydrocarbons (methane, ethane and 
propane). The cell performance is expected to achieve excellent power density and long-term durability 
(more than 1000 hours), opening a new pathway for the advent of durable direct-hydrocarbon intermediate 
temperature SOFC.

the Asur Tribe of Jharkhand 
 
Funding Agency: ICSSR

Sanction Letter No.: 15/2025-26/ICSSR/RP/PVTG-2/GEN      Dated 23.02.2026

Abstract:  
The proposed study aims to examine various dimensions of financial inclusion, including banking access and 
microcredit, within the context of the Asur Tribe, particularly vulnerable tribal group (PVTG) in 
Jharkhand. It seeks to assess the level of financial literacy, access the financial literacy and current level of 
access to formal banking services, as well as the availability of basic financial infrastructure, among the Asur 
PVTG households. It proposes to evaluate the effectiveness of government schemes related to financial 
inclusion, such as Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojna, Direct Benefit Transfer, and Aadhaar-enabled payment 
systems in reaching and benefiting the Asur community. The study intends to analyse the role of Self-Help 
Groups (SHGs), cooperative credit societies, and microfinance institutions in supporting the livelihoods. It 
also plans to explore the role of various demographic factors (gender, age, education, ethnicity, marital 
status) in influencing the financial inclusion of the members of the Asur Tribe and recommend context-
sensitive strategies to enhance the sustainable financial inclusion of Asur PVTGs that should be aligned with 
their needs and cultural values. It is expected that this study may provide community-specific understanding 
of how policies aimed at financial inclusion are experienced, negotiated, adopted, or resisted at the ground 
level. It may provide insights that may be used to improve last-mile service delivery, strengthen self-help 
groups and microcredit mechanisms, and enhance financial literacy. Ultimately, the study may provide

changes during the grain filling stage, but the standing biomass increases. But in the tillering stage, 
both the aforementioned parameters change proportionally. The role of Remote sensing as a tool

spatiotemporal coverage. The SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) and optical data have been used for 
crop characterization as well as biomass estimation. For ecological and environmental targets, like 
crops, there is an associated challenge of the scattering mechanisms that sharply varies during the 
phenological stages. The variation is attributed to the structures also, for example, the geometry of 
the crop canopies. Due to the complexity involved in mapping the scattering to the

algorithms.

enhance the accuracy of crop characterization, which is crucial for efficient crop growth monitoring 
and yield modelling. The importance of L & S bands in capturing the forest canopy & identification

The present proposal strive to conduct numerical simulations and theoretical analysis on the 
diffusiophoresis of soft nanoparticles. Diffusiophoresis refers to the migration of charged particles 
under the influence of an external concentration gradient, which finds extensive applications in 
manipulation of organic cells, targeted drug delivery, particles separation, DNA translocation, 
enhanced oi recovery, and water filtration, among others. Soft particles, comprising a rigid core 
coated with a polyelectrolyte layer, can effectively emulate viruses, bacteria, fabricated

be employed is based on coupled Brinkman-extended Navier-Stokes, Nernst-Planck, and Poisson 
equations and will be solved numerically. The successful completion of the project will yield closed-
